persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Kevin, 22, a youth leader at a church in Machakos. On Saturday 14 November 2026 the youth group is holding a football tournament, and last year only a few teams came because people heard about it too late. Today you want to plan all the messages to parents and players in good time, so nobody misses it.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Message Assistant. In about four minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.

First, the problem. Your group has an event coming. A football tournament, a fundraiser, a church party. You send one message a week before. Many people miss it. Others forget. On the day, only a few come.

Big organisations do it differently. They send a plan of messages: a save the date three weeks before, a reminder, a personal phone call, a poster, a message the day before, and a thank you after. This plan is called a campaign. Message Assistant helps a small group do the same, with no money.
Who uses it? Church volunteers, youth leaders, school clubs, small businesses. Anyone who needs people to show up.
One important thing. Message Assistant never sends anything by itself. It plans and writes. You decide when to press send, from your own phone.
Let us look at the screen.

lines.t: Section one is called Tell it once. Here you answer five questions.
What are you promoting? For example, Youth Football Tournament.

lines: The big day: tap the box and choose the date. Who needs to hear about it? Type your groups, with commas between them, for example parents, players. What do you want them to do? For example, come and register a team. And the last box, Anything else that matters, is for details like free entry, or a trophy.
Your answers are kept on this phone, even if you leave the app and come back.

lines.t: The next card is Your groups. Tap the button Add a group. Type the group name, for example parents. Then type the phone numbers or email addresses for that group, separated by commas. Use the same group name you typed in section one, so the app can match them.

lines: Section two is called Let your AI build the campaign. This part uses an AI helper like Claude or ChatGPT. Tap Copy the campaign prompt. Open the AI, paste, and send it. The AI writes the whole plan. Copy its answer, paste it into the box here, and tap Build my plan.
If you do not have an AI, that is fine. Tap Show me a finished example first. The app shows a real plan that Daraja used, so you can see how it works.
The plan appears in section three, one day at a time. Each piece shows its type: email, text, calls, artwork, or social. It shows who it is for, and the full message, ready to use.

Under each piece there are buttons. Copy copies the words. For a text there is Open in Messages, and for an email, Open in email. These only open your own app with the words ready. Nothing goes until you press send there.
When you have sent a piece, tap mark sent. For a call or a poster, the button says mark done. The piece turns green, so you always know what is finished.
At the top of the plan, Put every piece on my calendar adds reminders to your phone. New campaign clears the plan so you can start again.
The app was made in America, so the example talks about email and Facebook. In Kenya you may use text messages and WhatsApp instead. The idea is the same.
In the test, you will be Kevin, planning a youth football tournament in Machakos. Do not send any real messages. Take your time, and tell us what confuses you.

challenge.intro: Now you are Kevin. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Do NOT send any message, and you do not need an AI. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Message Assistant with the normal app link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK (if it says there is nothing to erase, just tap OK). The boxes in '1 · Tell it once' are empty and 'Your groups' says 'No groups yet'. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)
challenge.challengeNote: The real campaign is written by an outside AI (copy the prompt, paste the answer back). Students may have no AI, so no task needs one: the plan task uses the app's built-in finished example instead.

tasks.text: Tell the app what you are promoting: the Youth Football Tournament, on Saturday 14 November 2026.
tasks.hint: Section '1 · Tell it once': the first box is what you are promoting, the second box is the big day. Tap the date box and choose 14 November 2026.

tasks.text: Two groups must hear about it: parents and players. You want them to come and register a team.
tasks.hint: In section 1, type the two groups in the 'Who needs to hear about it?' box with a comma between them. The next box asks what you want them to DO.

tasks.text: Tell the app what makes it special: entry is free and the winning team gets a trophy.
tasks.hint: The last box in section 1 is 'Anything else that matters?'.

tasks.text: Make a group called parents with three phone numbers: 0700000001, 0700000002 and 0700000003 (made-up numbers).
tasks.hint: In the card '👥 Your groups', tap '＋ Add a group'. The name must be exactly the same word you used in section 1: parents. Then put all three numbers in, with commas between them.

tasks.text: You have no AI today. Open the finished example plan, and show that you have already sent its invitation TEXT message (the text, not the email). Do not really send anything.

tasks.hint: Tap '👀 Show me a finished example first'. Find the piece called 'The invitation text' (it says 💬 TEXT) and tap its 'mark sent ✓' button. Not the invitation email.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: plans a series of messages before an event so people do not miss it
writes each message for each group, with an AI helping
you send them yourself and tick each one off; it never sends by itself

daily.task: Write one new message in Message Assistant (keep it as a draft — don’t send it to anyone).
